sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya suṣeṇaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ avidhyan nakulaṃ ṣaṣṭyā sahadevaṃ ca saptabhiḥ
english: Then Suṣeṇa, beside himself with rage, took up another bow and pierced Nakula with sixty shafts and Sahadeva with seven.

sanskrit: tad yuddhaṃ sumahad ghoram āsīd devāsuropamam nighnatāṃ sāyakais tūrṇam anyonyasya vadhaṃ prati
english: That battle grew vast and terrible, like the war of gods and demons, as they swiftly struck one another with arrows, each bent on the other's death.

sanskrit: sātyakir vṛṣasenasya hatvā sūtaṃ tribhiḥ śaraiḥ dhanuś ciccheda bhallena jaghānāśvāṃś ca saptabhiḥ dhvajam ekeṣuṇonmathya tribhis taṃ hṛdy atāḍayat
english: Sātyaki, having slain Vṛṣasena's charioteer with three shafts, cut his bow with a broad arrow, killed his horses with seven, struck down his banner with a single dart, and pierced him in the heart with three.

sanskrit: athāvasannaḥ svarathe muhūrtāt punar utthitaḥ atho jighāṃsuḥ śaineyaṃ khaḍgacarmabhṛd abhyayāt
english: Then, having sunk down upon his own chariot, he rose again in a moment, and bearing sword and shield rushed at the scion of Śini, eager to slay him.

sanskrit: tasya cāplavataḥ śīghraṃ vṛṣasenasya sātyakiḥ varāhakarṇair daśabhir avidhyad asicarmaṇī
english: As Vṛṣasena came bounding swiftly forward, Sātyaki struck his sword and shield with ten boar-eared arrows.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanas tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā virathaṃ vyāyudhaṃ kṛtam āropya svarathe tūrṇam apovāha rathāntaram
english: But Duḥśāsana, seeing him stripped of chariot and weapon, took him up at once into his own car and bore him off to another chariot.

sanskrit: athānyaṃ ratham āsthāya vṛṣaseno mahārathaḥ karṇasya yudhi durdharṣaḥ punaḥ pṛṣṭham apālayat
english: Then, mounting another chariot, Vṛṣasena the great warrior, unassailable in battle, once more guarded Karṇa's rear.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanaṃ tu śaineyo navair navabhir āśugaiḥ visūtāśvarathaṃ kṛtvā lalāṭe tribhir ārpayat
english: And the scion of Śini, with nine and nine swift shafts, stripped Duḥśāsana of charioteer, horses, and car, and struck him with three upon the brow.

sanskrit: sa tv anyaṃ ratham āsthāya vidhivat kalpitaṃ punaḥ yuyudhe pāṇḍubhiḥ sārdhaṃ karṇasyāpyāyayan balam
english: But he, mounting another chariot duly equipped, fought once more against the Pāṇḍavas, swelling the strength of Karṇa's host.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tataḥ karṇam avidhyad daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ draupadeyās trisaptatyā yuyudhānas tu saptabhiḥ
english: Then Dhṛṣṭadyumna pierced Karṇa with ten shafts, the sons of Draupadī with seventy-three, and Yuyudhāna with seven.

sanskrit: bhīmasenaś catuḥṣaṣṭyā sahadevaś ca pañcabhiḥ nakulas triṃśatā bāṇaiḥ śatānīkaś ca saptabhiḥ śikhaṇḍī daśabhir vīro dharmarājaḥ śatena tu
english: Bhīmasena struck him with sixty-four, Sahadeva with five, Nakula with thirty arrows, Śatānīka with seven, the hero Śikhaṇḍin with ten, and the King of Righteousness with a hundred.

sanskrit: ete cānye ca rājendra pravīrā jayagṛddhinaḥ abhyardayan maheṣvāsaṃ sūtaputraṃ mahāmṛdhe
english: These and other foremost heroes, O lord of kings, greedy for victory, fell upon that mighty archer, the charioteer's son, in the great affray.

sanskrit: tān sūtaputro viśikhair daśabhir daśabhiḥ śitaiḥ rathe cāru caran vīraḥ pratyavidhyad ariṃdamaḥ
english: Them the charioteer's son, that valiant subduer of foes, ranging gracefully upon his car, pierced in return with ten and ten sharpened arrows each.

sanskrit: tatrāstravīryaṃ karṇasya lāghavaṃ ca mahātmanaḥ apaśyāma mahārāja tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: There, O great king, we beheld the might of Karṇa's weapons and the deftness of that high-souled one, and it seemed a thing of wonder.

sanskrit: na hy ādadānaṃ dadṛśuḥ saṃdadhānaṃ ca sāyakān vimuñcantaṃ ca saṃrambhād dadṛśus te mahāratham
english: For they could not see that great warrior taking up his arrows, nor fitting them to the string, nor loosing them in his fury.

sanskrit: dyaur viyad bhūr diśaś cāśu praṇunnā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ aruṇābhrāvṛtākāraṃ tasmin deśe babhau viyat
english: Heaven, sky, earth, and the quarters were swiftly overrun with his keen shafts; and in that place the firmament shone as if veiled with crimson cloud.

sanskrit: nṛtyann iva hi rādheyaś cāpahastaḥ pratāpavān yair viddhaḥ pratyavidhyat tān ekaikaṃ triguṇaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: As if dancing, bow in hand, the glorious son of Rādhā pierced in turn each of those by whom he had been struck, with thrice as many arrows.

sanskrit: daśabhir daśabhiś cainān punar viddhvā nanāda ha sāśvasūtadhvajacchatrās tatas te vivaraṃ daduḥ
english: And piercing them again with ten and ten apiece, he roared aloud; whereupon they, with their horses, charioteers, banners, and parasols, gave way and left him an opening.

sanskrit: tān pramṛdnan maheṣvāsān rādheyaḥ śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ rājānīkam asaṃbādhaṃ prāviśac chatrukarśanaḥ
english: Crushing those mighty archers with his showers of shafts, the son of Rādhā, tormentor of foes, entered the king's host where its ranks were thinnest.

sanskrit: sa rathāṃs triśatān hatvā cedīnām anivartinām rādheyo niśitair bāṇais tato 'bhyārcchad yudhiṣṭhiram
english: Having slain three hundred chariots of the unretreating Cedis, the son of Rādhā with his keen arrows then assailed Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: tatas te pāṇḍavā rājañ śikhaṇḍī ca sasātyakiḥ rādheyāt parirakṣanto rājānaṃ paryavārayan
english: Then those Pāṇḍavas, O king, with Śikhaṇḍin and Sātyaki, encircled the king to shield him from the son of Rādhā.

sanskrit: tathaiva tāvakāḥ sarve karṇaṃ durvāraṇaṃ raṇe yattāḥ senāmaheṣvāsāḥ paryarakṣanta sarvaśaḥ
english: In like manner all your own host, the great archers of the army, intent in battle, guarded Karṇa, irresistible in the fray, on every side.

sanskrit: nānāvāditraghoṣāś ca prādurāsan viśāṃ pate siṃhanādaś ca saṃjajñe śūrāṇām anivartinām
english: The blare of many instruments arose, O lord of peoples, and the lion-roar of the unretreating warriors broke forth.

sanskrit: tataḥ punaḥ samājagmur abhītāḥ kurupāṇḍavāḥ yudhiṣṭhiramukhāḥ pārthāḥ sūtaputramukhā vayam
english: Then once again the Kurus and Pāṇḍavas, fearless, came together — the sons of Pṛthā led by Yudhiṣṭhira, and we led by the charioteer's son.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca vidārya karṇas tāṃ senāṃ dharmarājam upādravat rathahastyaśvapattīnāṃ sahasraiḥ parivāritaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Karṇa, having rent that host asunder, rushed upon the King of Righteousness, surrounded by thousands of chariots, elephants, horsemen, and foot-soldiers.

sanskrit: nānāyudhasahasrāṇi preṣitāny aribhir vṛṣaḥ chittvā bāṇaśatair ugrais tān avidhyad asaṃbhramaḥ
english: The thousands of varied weapons hurled by his foes that bull among men cut apart with hundreds of fierce arrows, and, unperturbed, pierced his enemies in turn.

sanskrit: nicakarta śirāṃsy eṣāṃ bāhūn ūrūṃś ca sarvaśaḥ te hatā vasudhāṃ petur bhagnāś cānye vidudruvuḥ
english: He severed their heads, their arms, and their thighs on every side; slain, they fell to the earth, while others, broken, fled away.

sanskrit: draviḍāndhraniṣādās tu punaḥ sātyakicoditāḥ abhyardayañ jighāṃsantaḥ pattayaḥ karṇam āhave
english: But the Draviḍas, Andhras, and Niṣādas, urged on once more by Sātyaki, those foot-soldiers fell upon Karṇa in battle, seeking to slay him.

sanskrit: te vibāhuśirastrāṇāḥ prahatāḥ karṇasāyakaiḥ petuḥ pṛthivyāṃ yugapac chinnaṃ śālavanaṃ yathā
english: Stripped of arms, heads, and helmets, struck down by Karṇa's shafts, they fell upon the earth all at once, like a felled grove of sāla trees.

sanskrit: evaṃ yodhaśatāny ājau sahasrāṇy ayutāni ca hatānīyur mahīṃ dehair yaśasāpūrayan diśaḥ
english: Thus hundreds, thousands, and tens of thousands of warriors, slain in battle, sank to the earth in their bodies, filling the quarters with their fame.

sanskrit: atha vaikartanaṃ karṇaṃ raṇe kruddham ivāntakam rurudhuḥ pāṇḍupāñcālā vyādhiṃ mantrauṣadhair iva
english: Then the Pāṇḍavas and Pāñcālas hemmed in Karṇa Vaikartana, wrathful in battle like Death himself, as men hem in a disease with spells and herbs.

sanskrit: sa tān pramṛdyābhyapatat punar eva yudhiṣṭhiram mantrauṣadhikriyātīto vyādhir atyulbaṇo yathā
english: But crushing them, he fell once more upon Yudhiṣṭhira, like some most virulent disease that defies the remedy of spell and herb.

sanskrit: sa rājagṛddhibhī ruddhaḥ pāṇḍupāñcālakekayaiḥ nāśakat tān atikrāntuṃ mṛtyur brahmavido yathā
english: Hemmed in by the Pāṇḍavas, Pāñcālas, and Kekayas, all eager to seize the king, he could not break past them, as Death cannot pass a knower of Brahman.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiraḥ karṇam adūrasthaṃ nivāritam abravīt paravīraghnaḥ krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira, slayer of hostile heroes, his eyes red with wrath, spoke to Karṇa, who stood at no great distance, held in check.

sanskrit: karṇa karṇa vṛthādṛṣṭe sūtaputra vacaḥ śṛṇu sadā spardhasi saṃgrāme phalgunena yaśasvinā tathāsmān bādhase nityaṃ dhārtarāṣṭramate sthitaḥ
english: Karṇa, Karṇa of vain insight, son of a charioteer, hear my word! Ever in battle you vie with the glorious Phalguna, and ever you harry us, standing fast in the will of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son.

sanskrit: yad balaṃ yac ca te vīryaṃ pradveṣo yaś ca pāṇḍuṣu tat sarvaṃ darśayasvādya pauruṣaṃ mahad āsthitaḥ yuddhaśraddhāṃ sa te 'dyāhaṃ vineṣyāmi mahāhave
english: Whatever strength, whatever valor, and whatever hatred of the Pāṇḍavas is yours — show it all today, calling up your utmost manhood; for this day, in this great battle, I shall purge you of your appetite for war.

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahārāja karṇaṃ pāṇḍusutas tadā suvarṇapuṅkhair daśabhir vivyādhāyasmayaiḥ śitaiḥ
english: Having spoken thus, O great king, the son of Pāṇḍu then pierced Karṇa with ten keen iron arrows fledged with gold.

sanskrit: taṃ sūtaputro navabhiḥ pratyavidhyad ariṃdamaḥ vatsadantair maheṣvāsaḥ prahasann iva bhārata
english: The charioteer's son, that subduer of foes and mighty archer, pierced him in return with nine calf-toothed shafts, as though laughing, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṣurābhyāṃ pāñcālyau cakrarakṣau mahātmanaḥ jaghāna samare śūraḥ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: Then the hero, with two razor-tipped shafts and with smooth-jointed arrows, slew in battle the two Pāñcāla guardians of the high-souled king's chariot-wheels.

sanskrit: tāv ubhau dharmarājasya pravīrau paripārśvataḥ rathābhyāśe cakāśete candrasyeva punarvasū
english: Those two foremost heroes, on either flank of the King of Righteousness, had shone beside his chariot like the twin Punarvasu stars beside the moon.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraḥ punaḥ karṇam avidhyat triṃśatā śaraiḥ suṣeṇaṃ satyasenaṃ ca tribhis tribhir atāḍayat
english: Yudhiṣṭhira again pierced Karṇa with thirty shafts, and struck Suṣeṇa and Satyasena with three apiece.

sanskrit: śalyaṃ navatyā vivyādha trisaptatyā ca sūtajam tāṃś cāsya goptṝn vivyādha tribhis tribhir ajihmagaiḥ
english: He pierced Śalya with ninety arrows and the charioteer's son with seventy-three, and pierced those who guarded him with three straight-flying shafts each.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahasyādhirathir vidhunvānaḥ sa kārmukam bhittvā bhallena rājānaṃ viddhvā ṣaṣṭyānadan mudā
english: Then the son of Adhiratha, laughing and shaking his bow, cleft the king's bow with a broad arrow, pierced him with sixty shafts, and roared aloud in joy.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravīrāḥ pāṇḍūnām abhyadhāvan yudhiṣṭhiram sūtaputrāt parīpsantaḥ karṇam abhyardayañ śaraiḥ
english: Then the foremost heroes of the Pāṇḍavas ran toward Yudhiṣṭhira, seeking to save him from the charioteer's son, and assailed Karṇa with their arrows.

sanskrit: sātyakiś cekitānaś ca yuyutsuḥ pāṇḍya eva ca dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ śikhaṇḍī ca draupadeyāḥ prabhadrakāḥ
english: Sātyaki and Cekitāna, Yuyutsu and the Pāṇḍya, Dhṛṣṭadyumna and Śikhaṇḍin, the sons of Draupadī, and the Prabhadrakas;

sanskrit: yamau ca bhīmasenaś ca śiśupālasya cātmajaḥ kārūṣā matsyaśeṣāś ca kekayāḥ kāśikosalāḥ ete ca tvaritā vīrā vasuṣeṇam avārayan
english: the twins and Bhīmasena, and the son of Śiśupāla, the Karūṣas, the surviving Matsyas, the Kekayas, the Kāśis and Kosalas — these heroes, in haste, held Vasuṣeṇa in check.

sanskrit: janamejayaś ca pāñcālyaḥ karṇaṃ vivyādha sāyakaiḥ varāhakarṇair nārācair nālīkair niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ vatsadantair vipāṭhaiś ca kṣurapraiś caṭakāmukhaiḥ
english: And Janamejaya the Pāñcāla pierced Karṇa with his shafts — with boar-eared darts, iron arrows, tubular bolts, and keen arrows, with calf-toothed shafts, broad-headed darts, razor-edged and sparrow-mouthed arrows.

sanskrit: nānāpraharaṇaiś cograi rathahastyaśvasādinaḥ sarvato 'bhyādravan karṇaṃ parivārya jighāṃsayā
english: With diverse and dreadful weapons the riders of chariots, elephants, and horses rushed at Karṇa from every side, hemming him in with intent to kill.

sanskrit: sa pāṇḍavānāṃ pravaraiḥ sarvataḥ samabhidrutaḥ udairayad brāhmam astraṃ śaraiḥ saṃpūrayan diśaḥ
english: Beset on all sides by the foremost of the Pāṇḍavas, he invoked the Brahmā weapon, filling the quarters with his arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaramahājvālo vīryoṣmā karṇapāvakaḥ nirdahan pāṇḍavavanaṃ cāru paryacarad raṇe
english: Then the fire that was Karṇa, with arrows for its mighty flames and his valor for its heat, ranged gracefully through the battle, consuming the forest of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: sa saṃvārya mahāstrāṇi maheṣvāso mahātmanām prahasya puruṣendrasya śaraiś ciccheda kārmukam
english: That mighty archer, having turned aside the great weapons of those high-souled warriors, laughed and cut the bow of the lord of men with his shafts.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃdhāya navatiṃ nimeṣān nataparvaṇām bibheda kavacaṃ rājño raṇe karṇaḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then, fitting ninety smooth-jointed arrows in the twinkling of an eye, Karṇa with his keen shafts pierced through the king's armor in the battle.

sanskrit: tad varma hemavikṛtaṃ rarāja nipatat tadā savidyudabhraṃ savituḥ śiṣṭaṃ vātahataṃ yathā
english: That mail, wrought with gold, gleamed as it fell, like the remnant of a lightning-laden cloud, scattered by the wind from before the sun.

sanskrit: tad aṅgaṃ puruṣendrasya bhraṣṭavarma vyarocata ratnair alaṃkṛtaṃ divyair vyabhraṃ niśi yathā nabhaḥ
english: That body of the lord of men, its armor fallen away, shone adorned with celestial jewels, like the cloudless sky by night.

sanskrit: sa vivarmā śaraiḥ pārtho rudhireṇa samukṣitaḥ kruddhaḥ sarvāyasīṃ śaktiṃ cikṣepādhirathiṃ prati
english: Then the son of Pṛthā, stripped of mail by the arrows and drenched in blood, in his fury hurled an all-iron lance at the son of Adhiratha.

sanskrit: tāṃ jvalantīm ivākāśe śaraiś ciccheda saptabhiḥ sā chinnā bhūmim apatan maheṣvāsasya sāyakaiḥ
english: That lance, blazing as it were in the sky, he cut with seven arrows; severed by the mighty archer's shafts, it fell to the ground.

sanskrit: tato bāhvor lalāṭe ca hṛdi caiva yudhiṣṭhiraḥ caturbhis tomaraiḥ karṇaṃ tāḍayitvā mudānadat
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira, striking Karṇa upon both arms, upon the brow, and upon the heart with four javelins, roared aloud in joy.

sanskrit: udbhinnarudhiraḥ karṇaḥ kruddhaḥ sarpa iva śvasan dhvajaṃ ciccheda bhallena tribhir vivyādha pāṇḍavam iṣudhī cāsya ciccheda rathaṃ ca tilaśo 'cchinat
english: Karṇa, blood streaming forth, hissing in his wrath like a serpent, cut the banner with a broad arrow, pierced the Pāṇḍava with three, severed his two quivers, and shattered his chariot to bits.

sanskrit: evaṃ pārtho vyapāyāt sa nihataprārṣṭisārathiḥ aśaknuvan pramukhataḥ sthātuṃ karṇasya durmanāḥ
english: Thus the son of Pṛthā withdrew, his flank-guards and charioteer slain, unable, in his despair, to stand before Karṇa's face.

sanskrit: tam abhidrutya rādheyaḥ skandhaṃ saṃspṛśya pāṇinā abravīt prahasan rājan kutsayann iva pāṇḍavam
english: The son of Rādhā, rushing upon him, touched his shoulder with his hand and spoke, O king, laughing, as if to revile the Pāṇḍava:

sanskrit: kathaṃ nāma kule jātaḥ kṣatradharme vyavasthitaḥ prajahyāt samare śatrūn prāṇān rakṣan mahāhave
english: How should one born in a noble line, established in the warrior's duty, abandon his foes in combat to save his own life in the great battle?

sanskrit: na bhavān kṣatradharmeṣu kuśalo 'sīti me matiḥ brāhme bale bhavān yuktaḥ svādhyāye yajñakarmaṇi
english: It is my belief that you are not skilled in the duties of a warrior; you are suited rather to the strength of the brahmin — to study and the rites of sacrifice.

sanskrit: mā sma yudhyasva kaunteya mā ca vīrān samāsadaḥ mā cainān apriyaṃ brūhi mā ca vraja mahāraṇam
english: Do not fight, son of Kuntī; do not close with heroes, do not speak harsh words to them, and do not venture into the great battle.

sanskrit: evam uktvā tataḥ pārthaṃ visṛjya ca mahābalaḥ nyahanat pāṇḍavīṃ senāṃ vajrahasta ivāsurīm tataḥ prāyād drutaṃ rājan vrīḍann iva janeśvaraḥ
english: Having so spoken, the mighty one let the son of Pṛthā go and fell to smiting the Pāṇḍava host as the thunderbolt-bearer smites the demon hordes; then the lord of men, O king, departed swiftly, as if ashamed.

sanskrit: atha prayāntaṃ rājānam anvayus te tadācyutam cedipāṇḍavapāñcālāḥ sātyakiś ca mahārathaḥ draupadeyās tathā śūrā mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau
english: Then the Cedis, Pāṇḍavas, and Pāñcālas, and Sātyaki the great warrior, the valiant sons of Draupadī, and the two Pāṇḍava sons of Mādrī, followed the king as he withdrew, unshaken.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhirānīkaṃ dṛṣṭvā karṇaḥ parāṅmukham kurubhiḥ sahito vīraiḥ pṛṣṭhagaiḥ pṛṣṭham anvayāt
english: Then Karṇa, seeing Yudhiṣṭhira's host turned away in flight, pursued its rear together with the Kuru heroes who rode behind him.

sanskrit: śaṅkhabherīninādaiś ca kārmukāṇāṃ ca nisvanaiḥ babhūva dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ siṃhanādaravas tadā
english: Then, with the blare of conches and kettledrums and the twang of bows, the lion-roar of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons arose.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras tu kauravya ratham āruhya satvaraḥ śrutakīrter mahārāja dṛṣṭavān karṇavikramam
english: But Yudhiṣṭhira, O scion of Kuru, mounting in haste the chariot of Śrutakīrti, O great king, looked upon Karṇa's prowess.

sanskrit: kālyamānaṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭvā dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ tān yodhān abravīt kruddho hatainaṃ vai sahasraśaḥ
english: Seeing his host driven before the foe, the King of Righteousness, Yudhiṣṭhira, wrathful, said to those warriors: Slay him! Slay him by the thousand!

sanskrit: tato rājñābhyanujñātāḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathāḥ bhīmasenamukhāḥ sarve putrāṃs te pratyupādravan
english: Then, given leave by the king, the great warriors of the Pāṇḍavas, all led by Bhīmasena, charged against your sons.

sanskrit: abhavat tumulaḥ śabdo yodhānāṃ tatra bhārata hastyaśvarathapattīnāṃ śastrāṇāṃ ca tatas tataḥ
english: There arose a tumultuous din of warriors, O Bhārata — of elephants, horses, chariots, and foot-soldiers, and of weapons, on every side.

sanskrit: uttiṣṭhata praharata praitābhipatateti ca iti bruvāṇā anyonyaṃ jaghnur yodhā raṇājire
english: Rise! Strike! Advance! Fall upon them! — so crying out to one another, the warriors slew each other on the field of battle.

sanskrit: abhracchāyeva tatrāsīc charavṛṣṭibhir ambare samāvṛttair naravarair nighnadbhir itaretaram
english: There, from the showers of arrows in the air, came a darkness as of cloud-shadow, as the foremost of men, met together, struck one another down.

sanskrit: vipatākādhvajacchatrā vyaśvasūtāyudhā raṇe vyaṅgāṅgāvayavāḥ petuḥ kṣitau kṣīṇā hateśvarāḥ
english: Bereft of pennons, banners, and parasols, of horses, charioteers, and weapons, their limbs mangled, their lords slain, the spent warriors fell upon the ground.

sanskrit: pravarāṇīva śailānāṃ śikharāṇi dvipottamāḥ sārohā nihatāḥ petur vajrabhinnā ivādrayaḥ
english: The noblest of elephants, like the towering peaks of mountains, fell slain with their riders, like crags split by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: chinnabhinnaviparyastair varmālaṃkāravigrahaiḥ sārohās turagāḥ petur hatavīrāḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: Horses by the thousand, their armor and trappings cut, broken, and overturned, fell with their riders, their heroes slain.

sanskrit: vipraviddhāyudhāṅgāś ca dviradāśvarathair hatāḥ prativīraiś ca saṃmarde pattisaṃghāḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: And bands of foot-soldiers by the thousand, their weapons and limbs scattered about, were slain in the press by elephants, horses, chariots, and by hostile warriors.

sanskrit: viśālāyatatāmrākṣaiḥ padmendusadṛśānanaiḥ śirobhir yuddhaśauṇḍānāṃ sarvataḥ saṃstṛtā mahī
english: On every side the earth was strewn with the heads of battle-drunken warriors — heads with broad, long, coppery eyes and faces like the lotus and the moon.

sanskrit: tathā tu vitate vyomni nisvanaṃ śuśruvur janāḥ vimānair apsaraḥsaṃghair gītavāditranisvanaiḥ
english: And in the wide expanse of the heavens men heard a sound — the celestial cars of the throngs of Apsarases and the strains of their song and music.

sanskrit: hatān kṛttān abhimukhān vīrān vīraiḥ sahasraśaḥ āropyāropya gacchanti vimāneṣv apsarogaṇāḥ
english: The heroes slain and cut down while facing the foe — by the thousand the hosts of Apsarases bore them up, one by one, into their celestial cars, and departed.
